intent.user_prompt: Build an 8-bit event-counting subsystem as a complete SR2FPGA Verilog RTL project. This is component topology t1_event_counter, difficulty tier T1. Use an event_gate in front of a counter_core. The design must implement this black-box behavior: event_valid pulses pass through an event gate and increment the counter core. Keep rtl/top.v as the integration wrapper and keep each reusable component in a separate RTL file. Preserve these interface contracts: top.event_valid -> event_gate.event_valid; event_gate.count_en -> counter_core.en; counter_core.count -> top.count. Include system_his.json, manifest.json, timing constraints, predicted QoR, and a bounded self-checking testbench that prints TEST_PASS only on success or TEST_FAIL on failure.
intent.design_goal: 8-bit event-counting subsystem comprising an event_gate and a counter_core.
assumptions: event_valid is synchronous to clk and deasserted after one cycle
rst_n is active low and asserted for at least one cycle to clear the counter
the counter wraps when overflow occurs

components.name: event_gate
components.intent: Produces a one-cycle pulse on count_en whenever event_valid is high, synchronized to clk, and gated by reset.

components.name: counter_core
components.intent: 8-bit up counter that increments by one on cycles where en is high, synchronous to clk, reset to 0.

timing.throughput: one event per cycle

scenarios.name: basic_counting
scenarios.description: After reset, apply a sequence of event_valid pulses and verify the count increments correctly.

verification.pass_condition: testbench prints TEST_PASS and no TEST_FAIL

intent.user_prompt: Build an 8-bit valid-ready stream fork datapath as a complete SR2FPGA Verilog RTL project. This is component topology t3_stream_fork, difficulty tier T3. Use a skid_buffer feeding a stream_fork and two stream_stage outputs. The design must implement this black-box behavior: valid input samples pass through a skid buffer and are duplicated to two output stages. Keep rtl/top.v as the integration wrapper and keep each reusable component in a separate RTL file. Preserve these interface contracts: top.in_valid -> skid_buffer.in_valid; top.in_data -> skid_buffer.in_data; skid_buffer.out_valid -> stream_fork.in_valid; skid_buffer.out_data -> stream_fork.in_data; stream_fork.in_ready -> skid_buffer.out_ready; stream_fork.out0_valid -> stream_stage.in_valid; stream_fork.out0_data -> stream_stage.in_data; stream_stage.in_ready -> stream_fork.out0_ready; stream_fork.out1_valid -> stream_stage.in_valid; stream_fork.out1_data -> stream_stage.in_data; stream_stage.in_ready -> stream_fork.out1_ready; stream_stage.out_valid -> top.out0_valid; stream_stage.out_data -> top.out0_data; stream_stage.out_valid -> top.out1_valid; stream_stage.out_data -> top.out1_data. Include system_his.json, manifest.json, timing constraints, predicted QoR, and a bounded self-checking testbench that prints TEST_PASS only on success or TEST_FAIL on failure.
intent.design_goal: Implement a reliable, backpressure-tolerant stream fork that duplicates an 8-bit valid-ready input to two independent output streams, using a skid buffer for input elasticity and pipeline stages for output registration.
assumptions: All components share the same clock domain
External ready signals are well-behaved (no combinational loops)
Data width is fixed at 8 bits

components.name: skid_buffer
components.intent: Provides one-entry skid buffer to decouple input backpressure from the fork, allowing full throughput when possible and storing one data word when downstream stalls.

components.name: stream_fork
components.intent: Duplicates the incoming valid-ready stream to two independent output streams. The input is acknowledged only when both outputs are ready.

components.name: stream_stage
components.intent: Registers the valid and data signals, adding one cycle of latency. Used to provide clean output timing and isolate output backpressure.

intent.user_prompt: Build an 8-bit streaming accumulator datapath as a complete SR2FPGA Verilog RTL project. This is component topology t2_stream_accumulator, difficulty tier T2. Use a skid_buffer feeding an accumulator_core. The design must implement this black-box behavior: valid input samples pass through a skid buffer and accumulate into the running sum. Keep rtl/top.v as the integration wrapper and keep each reusable component in a separate RTL file. Preserve these interface contracts: top.in_valid -> skid_buffer.in_valid; top.in_data -> skid_buffer.in_data; skid_buffer.out_valid -> accumulator_core.sample_valid; skid_buffer.out_data -> accumulator_core.sample; accumulator_core.sample_ready -> skid_buffer.out_ready; accumulator_core.sum -> top.sum. Include system_his.json, manifest.json, timing constraints, predicted QoR, and a bounded self-checking testbench that prints TEST_PASS only on success or TEST_FAIL on failure.
intent.design_goal: Compose an 8-bit streaming accumulator using a skid buffer and accumulator core, with top-level integration and proper handshaking.
assumptions: The accumulator always has sample_ready = 1 (no backpressure from accumulator).
Sum register width matches data width (8 bits) and wraps on overflow.

ports.name: sample_valid
ports.description: Output sum valid (high when new sum available)

components.name: skid_buffer
components.intent: Standard skid buffer for pipelining data with backpressure. When in_valid and in_ready, captures in_data into internal register and asserts out_valid. When out_valid and out_ready, deasserts out_valid.

components.name: accumulator_core
components.intent: 8-bit accumulator: on each cycle where sample_valid_in is high, adds sample to internal sum register. sample_ready is always high. sample_valid output mirrors sample_valid_in (combinational).

data_flow.description: Data path from input to accumulated sum output

data_flow.description: Valid signal chain from input valid to output sample_valid

data_flow.description: Back-pressure ready signal from accumulator back to top input

scenarios.description: Send sequence 1,2,3; expect sum = 6 after last sample, with correct sample_valid assertion.

scenarios.name: overflow_wrap
scenarios.description: Send sequence 100 + 200; 8-bit sum wraps to 44 (300 mod 256 = 44).

scenarios.name: backpressure_idle
scenarios.description: No input for several cycles; sum remains unchanged.

Stream stages each provide one register on data and valid signals

components.intent: One-deep skid buffer that registers incoming data to improve timing, with full valid/ready backpressure.

components.name: stream_fork
components.intent: Duplicates a valid/ready input stream to two identical output streams, asserting out_valid only when both output ready signals are high.

scenarios.name: basic_transfer
scenarios.description: Send one sample with all ready signals high, check that both outputs receive the sample after 2 cycles.
scenarios.stimuli: Drive in_valid high with in_data=0x55 for 1 cycle, hold out0_ready and out1_ready high.
scenarios.checks: After latency, out0_data==0x55 and out1_data==0x55, out0_valid and out1_valid high.

scenarios.name: backpressure_out0
scenarios.description: Deassert out0_ready while out1_ready high; verify that both outputs stall (fork requires both ready).
scenarios.stimuli: Send sample, then hold out0_ready low.
scenarios.checks: No new valid on either output while out0_ready low.

scenarios.name: backpressure_out1
scenarios.description: Deassert out1_ready while out0_ready high; verify stall.
scenarios.stimuli: Send sample, then hold out1_ready low.
scenarios.checks: No new valid on either output while out1_ready low.

scenarios.name: consecutive_transfers
scenarios.description: Transfer multiple samples back-to-back.
scenarios.stimuli: Drive in_valid continuously with changing data, keep both out_readys high.
scenarios.checks: Each data appears on both outputs two cycles later, no dropped samples.

intent.design_goal: Implement an 8-bit dual-stream join datapath with two skid buffers, a stream join unit, an accumulator, and an output pipeline stage. The design must correctly handle valid-ready handshakes, buffer and synchronize the two input streams, join them into a single stream, accumulate results, and present the final output with a register stage.
assumptions: Joined data width is 16 bits (concatenation of two 8-bit inputs)
Accumulator sum width is 9 bits (DATA_WIDTH+1) to avoid overflow, configurable via ACCUM_WIDTH
All valid-ready interfaces follow standard handshake: transfer occurs when both valid and ready are high at the same cycle
Skid buffers can store at most one data beat
Stream join is combinational: asserts out_valid only when both inputs are valid and output ready is high, and produces joined data immediately
Accumulator adds the received joined sample to its internal sum register on each valid transfer
Stream stage is a single pipeline register with valid/ready handshake
Testbench will drive random stimulus with backpressure and verify functional correctness

components.intent: Provides a skid buffer that can absorb one beat while backpressured, ensuring lossless transfer

components.intent: Accumulates incoming samples by adding them to an internal sum register, asserting sum_valid when a new sum is available

components.name: stream_stage
components.intent: Inserts a single register stage with skid capability, preserving the valid-ready protocol and adding one cycle of latency
